title: nixos/dokuwiki: Remove unused enable option
reason: Applicable, and the coordinator's own flagged case: real dokuwiki module + wired test (dokuwiki = handleTest ./dokuwiki.nix {}; at head). Real diff GENUINELY REMOVES the per-site `enable = mkEnableOption "DokuWiki web application";` declaration (services.dokuwiki.sites.<name>.enable, a wildcard-instance option), replacing it with an imports-based throw-on-use deprecation shim plus an assertion -- an unusual removal mechanism (not mkRemovedOptionModule, a custom throw+assertion pattern) but a genuine option lifecycle event, through a wildcard-instance form.
targets_toml: single target dokuwiki, cfg_ident=cfg, option_prefix=[services,dokuwiki,sites,*] (wildcard attrsOf-submodule-instance form), watch=[enable] (the removed option, deliberately, to compare against sshd's moduliFile case).

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: DIRECT ANSWER to the flagged question: this lands in the SAME rendering-gap bucket as sshd's moduliFile (predicate_not_found->option_not_found), not a different/new class -- raw.json summary shows changed=1 with the correct transition, summary.md is all-zero, notable=[]. Running tally for this specific direction (predicate_not_found->option_not_found): sshd/B2, this one/B5 = 2 instances; combined with the option_not_found->predicate_not_found direction (cockpit/B3, rspamd+prowlarr/B4, onlyoffice-documentserver/B5 = 4), the rendering gap is now at 6 total instances across 6 modules, both transition directions, both plain top-level AND wildcard-instance option forms.

SEPARATE positive data point worth noting: unlike wstunnel's PR415326 (base 4) where a real wildcard-instance option was OptionNotFound at BOTH sides (undetected even at base, consistent with S4's own documented wildcard-attrsOf gap), here at BASE the wildcard resolution correctly found `enable` (PredicateNotFound, not OptionNotFound) -- so wildcard-instance declaration discovery is not uniformly broken, it worked here. Not asserting why the two cases differ (possibly wstunnel's specific commonOptions-merge-into-multiple-parents shape vs dokuwiki's more standard single attrsOf(submodule) siteOpts shape) -- flagging the discrepancy for the coordinator rather than guessing at the mechanism.
